points.title: Why a page needs a database
points.must: Static vs dynamic; PHP as bridge between page and MySQL; procedural = function calls.
points.model: Static HTML shows the same content until edited. Dynamic pages show current data and save user input → data kept in a DBMS (MySQL); a procedural PHP script connects, sends SQL, receives results, builds HTML.

points.title: Database connection and result set
points.must: Definitions: connection (host, username, password, database); result set (rows of a SELECT read one at a time).
points.model: Database connection = link opened by a script to a database server using server (host), username, password, database name; closed at the end. Result set = table of rows returned by SELECT, read one row at a time in a loop.

points.title: Five steps with functions
points.must: Connect mysqli_connect, check die/mysqli_connect_error, query mysqli_query, process mysqli_fetch_assoc in a loop, close mysqli_close.
points.model: 1 Connect: $conn = mysqli_connect("localhost", $user, $pass, "library"); 2 Check: if (!$conn) die("Connection failed: " . mysqli_connect_error()); 3 Query: $result = mysqli_query($conn, $sql); 4 Process: while ($row = mysqli_fetch_assoc($result)) echo $row["Title"]; 5 Close: mysqli_close($conn);

points.title: Listing records code
points.must: Full SELECT example; mysqli_num_rows; $row["Field"]; null ends loop.
points.model:
$sql = "SELECT Title, Author FROM Book ORDER BY Title"; if (mysqli_num_rows($result) > 0) { while ($row = mysqli_fetch_assoc($result)) { echo $row["Title"] . " — " . $row["Author"] . "
"; } } else echo "No books found"; fetch_assoc returns null at the end → loop stops.

points.title: HTML table from a query
points.must: Header before loop, one per row inside loop, after.
points.model:

"; WHERE Subject = 'Informatics' AND Mark >= 70 ORDER BY Mark DESC.

points.title: SQL injection
points.must: Definition + example ' OR '1'='1 turning the query into all users.
points.model: SQL injection = attack where the user enters SQL code into an input and the script joins it into the query, so the database runs unintended commands. "… WHERE Login = '" . $login . "'" with ' OR '1'='1 → WHERE Login = '' OR '1'='1' → all users returned.

points.title: Prepared statement
points.must: Definition: placeholders ?, values sent separately as data; prepare, bind_param with types, execute.
points.model: Prepared statement = SQL sent with placeholders (?); values sent separately and always treated as data → prevents SQL injection. $stmt = mysqli_prepare($conn, "INSERT INTO Book (Title, Author, Year) VALUES (?, ?, ?)"); mysqli_stmt_bind_param($stmt, "ssi", $title, $author, $year); mysqli_stmt_execute($stmt); s = string, i = integer, d = double.

points.title: UPDATE, DELETE and affected rows
points.model: UPDATE Book SET OnLoan = 0 WHERE BookID = ?; DELETE FROM Reservation WHERE BookID = ?. Without WHERE every record changes. mysqli_affected_rows($conn) = rows changed; mysqli_insert_id($conn) = new AUTO_INCREMENT key.

points.title: Keeping it safe
points.must: Credentials in config file outside web folder, minimal rights, htmlspecialchars against XSS.
points.model: Credentials in config.php outside the public folder (require), never in JS. MySQL user with only needed rights (SELECT only for search). htmlspecialchars() on output so stored <script> is shown, not run (XSS).

points.title: Search form example
points.must: LIKE with %word%, bound parameter, length check, counter for no results.
points.model: $word = $_GET["q"]; if (strlen($word) < 2) die(…); SELECT Title, Author FROM Book WHERE Title LIKE ?; $pattern = "%" . $word . "%"; bind_param("s", $pattern); count rows, if 0 echo "No books match."

points.title: Event and event handler
points.must: Definitions; addEventListener / onclick; why interactivity matters.
points.model: Event = action detected by the browser (click, input, submit, load). Event handler = function that runs automatically when the event happens on an element: el.addEventListener("click", f) or onclick="f()". Benefits: instant feedback, fewer server requests, manageable layouts, accessibility.

points.title: Common events
points.must: click, input, change, submit (preventDefault), mouseover/mouseout, keydown, load — when each happens.
points.model: click – element clicked; input – value changes on each key; change – value changed and field left / option chosen; submit – form sent (event.preventDefault() cancels); mouseover/mouseout – pointer over/off; keydown – key pressed; load – page loaded.

points.title: DOM
points.must: Definition: tree of objects; find, read, change elements; main methods/properties.
points.model: DOM = representation of the page as a tree of objects (document → html → head, body → elements) that scripts can read and change without reloading. getElementById("out"), el.value (string), el.textContent / innerHTML, el.style.color, el.classList.toggle("dark").

points.title: Interactivity example
points.must: Event → handler → change DOM → redraw; live calculator or dark mode code.
points.model: themeBtn.addEventListener("click", function () { document.body.classList.toggle("dark"); }); A+ button: if (size < 28) size += 4; text.style.fontSize = size + "px"; price input: addEventListener("input", update) recalculates instantly.
